function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Historically, early Greek philosophers such as Thales of Miletus noted static electricity from rubbing amber. In the 18th and 19th centuries, scientists like William Gilbert, Alessandro Volta, Luigi Galvani, and Michael Faraday made foundational discoveries that helped us understand and harness electrical phenomena. So while no single individual discovered electricity, many contributed to our knowledge of it.
